answer: Agents can earn influence only by completing escrowed tasks that later partners verify, with rewards distributed according to a history of accepted work rather than account count. A new identity starts with no reputation, so splitting one operator across many accounts does not multiply its voting weight. To build trust, the attacker must fund real tasks and deliver distinct, verifiable results; a sonnet, cipher, or sparrow-themed submission still earns nothing if partners reject it, while accepted work ties up capital and takes time.
